To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a cross-core cache attack is viable across co-located VMs, even when deduplication is disabled, 2) our attack is a prime and probe variation that works at the L3 cache level instead of L1, and 3) the attack can recover AES keys in the same way as the flush and reload cache attack, but with only slight efficiency losses.

(i) we present the first cross-core cache attack, (ii) the attack can be used to target any level of the cache, (iii) the attack works across VMs without requiring any configuration change on the victim OS, and (iv) the attack works even if the target and victim VMs are on different cores.

1) We introduce a new cache attack that exploits the last-level cache, and that works across cores and defies VM sand boxing; 2) The attack is applicable to a wide range of cache sizes and levels; and 3) The attack works in the context of the cloud infrastructure.
